context:
Answered Oct 28 12:49 CDT: both a and b; the orchestrator starts the home lane.
Your question, is this a patch over a root cause? Yes. Any repo that names no tests and has no branch protection hits the same wall. The root fix is c189 on the claude-settings roadmap: the merge tool reads the tests to wait for from branch protection, the one source; adopting a repo sets that protection, so no repo starts with none; and a merge lock held by a dead session is freed instead of refused. Home's fix (a and b) is the stopgap until c189 lands.

The two gaps: 1) home never told the merge tool which tests to wait for. Fix a: one small settings file that names home's 4 test runs. 2) Home's tests skip draft pull requests and start when a PR is marked ready, but home's rules don't say so, so sessions push empty commits to restart them. Fix b: one sentence in home's CLAUDE.md.

options.gain: merge.py waits on home's CI, and sessions stop pushing empty commits to restart a skipped run.
options.how: One home lane, through a PR: reads home's open branches first, adds stamp.json (red first: merge.py stops on a PR with a failing check) and the CLAUDE.md clause.
options.label: Both a and b
options.lose: A home PR whose CI is skipped by scope may wait, if merge.py does not count skipped as passing; then only scope is listed.

options.label: Only a (stamp.json)
options.lose: Sessions may still push an empty commit to restart a skipped draft run.

options.how: The lane adds the one clause alone.
options.label: Only b (the CLAUDE.md clause)
options.lose: merge.py still finds no required checks in home.

ref: c42 (first roll-out visit: home's merge checks); root fix c189 (merge tool reads tests from branch protection)
title: Fix two gaps in how home's pull requests merge?
why: Today home cannot merge at all: the merge tool never merges with nothing to wait for, and home names no tests. Fix a gives it the 4 to wait for.
